flagged.evidence: The Statement requires the length identity for all 0≤r≤q≤L, while step 6.1 proceeds: “Now let r=ρ₀<…<ρ_N=q be a partition of [r,q].” No such strict partition exists when r=q. The singleton-interval convention in the Statement immediately supplies the identity in that case, so this is an omitted endpoint branch.

The induction treats the mixed case only as “x∈ι_e(C_e), y∈Z₁,” while claiming injectivity of z↦d₀(x,z) for every ordered pair. For the opposite ordering, swapping endpoints gives injectivity of distance from y; to obtain the claimed injectivity from x one also needs d₀(x,z)=d₀(x,y)−d₀(y,z) for z∈I(x,y). This follows immediately from the definition of I, so the gap is nonfatal.
